subject: Maternity
stem: A nurse is counseling a woman at her first prenatal visit at 8 weeks gestation. Which statement by the nurse best supports neural tube defect prevention?

options.text: Take 400 to 800 mcg of folic acid daily throughout early pregnancy
options.feedback: Correct. Adequate folic acid before and during early pregnancy reduces neural tube defect risk.

options.text: Increase your daily vitamin A intake with liver several times a week
options.feedback: Incorrect. Excess preformed vitamin A is teratogenic.

options.text: Begin iron supplementation only if you become anemic in the third trimester
options.feedback: Incorrect. This does not address neural tube defects.

options.text: Limit all leafy green vegetables to reduce nausea
options.feedback: Incorrect. Leafy greens are a folate source and should be encouraged.

rationale: Folic acid supplementation in early pregnancy is the key preventive measure against neural tube defects.

subject: Pediatrics
stem: A parent brings an 18-month-old for a well-child visit. Which finding should the nurse recognize as expected for this age?

options.text: Walks up stairs with one hand held and says several single words
options.feedback: Correct. These are typical 18-month gross-motor and language milestones.

options.text: Speaks in three-word sentences and rides a tricycle
options.feedback: Incorrect. These are closer to 3-year milestones.

options.text: Sits without support but does not yet crawl
options.feedback: Incorrect. This suggests around 6 months and would be delayed.

options.text: Builds a tower of eight cubes and copies a circle
options.feedback: Incorrect. These are preschool-age skills.

rationale: At 18 months a toddler walks up stairs with a hand held and uses single words, consistent with normal development.

subject: Community Health
stem: A 66-year-old client with no chronic illness asks which vaccines are recommended at this age. Which response by the nurse is most accurate?

options.text: You should receive the pneumococcal vaccine and an annual influenza vaccine
options.feedback: Correct. Pneumococcal vaccination and annual influenza are recommended for adults 65 and older.

options.text: No further vaccines are needed once you are over 65
options.feedback: Incorrect. Older adults have specific recommended vaccines.

options.text: You only need a tetanus booster every 20 years
options.feedback: Incorrect. Td boosters are every 10 years and this ignores other vaccines.

options.text: Live vaccines such as MMR should be repeated yearly
options.feedback: Incorrect. MMR is not an annual vaccine for adults.

rationale: Adults 65 and older are advised to receive pneumococcal and annual influenza vaccination.

subject: Maternity
stem: A postpartum client who is breastfeeding reports sore, cracked nipples on day 3. Which teaching point should the nurse emphasize first?

options.text: Ensure the infant latches with the areola, not just the nipple, in the mouth
options.feedback: Correct. Poor latch is the most common cause of nipple trauma.

options.text: Limit each feeding to five minutes per breast
options.feedback: Incorrect. Time limits do not fix the underlying latch problem.

options.text: Switch to formula until the nipples heal completely
options.feedback: Incorrect. Stopping breastfeeding is unnecessary and not first-line.

options.text: Wash the nipples with soap before each feeding
options.feedback: Incorrect. Soap dries and worsens cracking.

rationale: Correcting the latch so the areola is in the infant's mouth resolves most nipple soreness.

subject: Community Health
stem: A 52-year-old client with no family history of cancer asks about recommended screenings. Which screening should the nurse discuss as newly due at this age?

options.text: Colorectal cancer screening
options.feedback: Correct. Average-risk colorectal screening is recommended beginning at age 45 to 50.

options.text: Annual bone density scanning
options.feedback: Incorrect. Routine DEXA screening typically begins later, at 65 for women.

options.text: Yearly abdominal aortic aneurysm ultrasound for all adults
options.feedback: Incorrect. AAA screening is a one-time test for certain men who smoked.

options.text: Prostate biopsy for every man over 50
options.feedback: Incorrect. Biopsy is not a screening test.

rationale: Colorectal cancer screening is recommended for average-risk adults starting at 45 to 50 years.

subject: Pediatrics
stem: A nurse teaches parents of a 4-month-old about injury prevention. Which instruction is most appropriate for this developmental stage?

options.text: Never leave the infant unattended on a changing table or bed
options.feedback: Correct. At 4 months infants begin rolling, creating a fall risk.

options.text: Place soft pillows around the infant in the crib for comfort
options.feedback: Incorrect. Soft bedding increases suffocation and SIDS risk.

options.text: Begin using a forward-facing car seat
options.feedback: Incorrect. Infants remain rear-facing well beyond this age.

options.text: Allow the infant to hold small solid finger foods
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is a choking hazard and premature.

rationale: Because 4-month-olds start to roll, never leaving them unattended on elevated surfaces prevents falls.

subject: Mental Health
stem: During a routine visit, a nurse administers a depression screening tool to an adult client. Which client response most warrants immediate further assessment?

options.text: Reports recent thoughts that life is not worth living
options.feedback: Correct. Any indication of suicidal ideation requires immediate follow-up.

options.text: States feeling tired more often since starting a new job
options.feedback: Incorrect. Fatigue alone is nonspecific and not urgent.

options.text: Describes occasional worry about finances
options.feedback: Incorrect. Situational worry is common and not an emergency.

options.text: Mentions eating slightly less on busy days
options.feedback: Incorrect. Minor appetite variation is not urgent.

rationale: A positive screen for suicidal ideation requires immediate, focused safety assessment.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: A nurse plans discharge teaching for a newly diagnosed diabetic client. Which client cue best indicates readiness to learn?

options.text: The client asks how to prepare the insulin syringe correctly
options.feedback: Correct. Asking task-specific questions signals engagement and readiness.

options.text: The client is in severe pain and requesting medication
options.feedback: Incorrect. Unmet physical needs impair learning readiness.

options.text: The client states there is no need to learn any of this
options.feedback: Incorrect. This reflects a barrier, not readiness.

options.text: The client is drowsy from recent sedation
options.feedback: Incorrect. Reduced alertness impairs learning.

rationale: A client who initiates relevant questions demonstrates motivation and readiness to learn.

subject: Community Health
stem: A client who smokes a pack of cigarettes daily tells the nurse, 'I have been thinking maybe I should quit one of these days.' Which response best supports this client's stage of change?

options.text: What benefits do you think quitting could bring you?
options.feedback: Correct. Exploring perceived benefits fits a contemplative client and strengthens motivation.

options.text: Here is a schedule to taper your cigarettes starting today
options.feedback: Incorrect. An action plan is premature before commitment.

options.text: You must stop smoking immediately to avoid lung cancer
options.feedback: Incorrect. Confrontation can raise resistance at this stage.

options.text: Since you are not ready, we will revisit this in a year
options.feedback: Incorrect. Dismissing the opening misses a motivational opportunity.

rationale: A client contemplating change benefits from exploring personal benefits, which builds intrinsic motivation.

subject: Maternity
stem: A nurse provides education to a client at 28 weeks gestation about warning signs to report. Which symptom, if reported, requires the most urgent evaluation?

options.text: Severe headache with visual changes and swelling of the face
options.feedback: Correct. These suggest preeclampsia and require urgent evaluation.

options.text: Occasional mild lower back ache after standing
options.feedback: Incorrect. Mild back ache is common in pregnancy.

options.text: Increased clear vaginal discharge without odor
options.feedback: Incorrect. Increased leukorrhea is normal.

options.text: Feeling fetal movements several times a day
options.feedback: Incorrect. Regular fetal movement is reassuring.

rationale: Severe headache, visual disturbances, and facial edema are classic warning signs of preeclampsia.

subject: Community Health
stem: A home-health nurse assesses a 78-year-old client living alone. Which finding is the priority to address for fall prevention?

options.text: Loose throw rugs on the walkway between rooms
options.feedback: Correct. Loose rugs are a leading modifiable home fall hazard.

options.text: A calendar of upcoming medical appointments on the wall
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is unrelated to fall risk.

options.text: A landline telephone in the kitchen
options.feedback: Incorrect. A phone is a communication resource, not a hazard.

options.text: Family photographs displayed on a bookshelf
options.feedback: Incorrect. This poses no fall risk.

rationale: Removing loose throw rugs eliminates a common and easily corrected home fall hazard.

subject: Pediatrics
stem: A parent asks when to begin introducing solid foods to their healthy infant. Which response by the nurse is most appropriate?

options.text: Around 6 months, when the infant can sit with support and shows interest in food
options.feedback: Correct. Developmental readiness around 6 months guides solid introduction.

options.text: At 2 months, adding cereal to the bottle to help sleep
options.feedback: Incorrect. Early solids and cereal in bottles are not recommended.

options.text: Only after the first birthday to avoid all allergies
options.feedback: Incorrect. Delaying to 12 months is not recommended.

options.text: Whenever the infant doubles the birth weight, regardless of age
options.feedback: Incorrect. Weight alone does not determine readiness.

rationale: Solid foods are introduced around 6 months when developmental readiness signs appear.

subject: Maternity
stem: A nurse teaches a pregnant client about common discomforts and self-care. Which self-care measures are appropriate to include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Rise slowly from lying to standing to reduce dizziness
Eat small frequent meals to ease nausea
Elevate the legs periodically to relieve dependent edema
Perform pelvic tilt exercises for low back discomfort
Restrict all fluids to prevent frequent urination
Take over-the-counter medications freely for any symptom

rationale: Positional changes, small meals, leg elevation, and pelvic tilts are safe measures; fluid restriction and unsupervised medication use are not.

subject: Community Health
stem: A nurse counsels an adult with prehypertension on lifestyle changes. Which recommendations are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Reduce dietary sodium intake
Engage in regular aerobic physical activity
Limit alcohol consumption
Maintain a healthy body weight
Increase intake of processed and canned foods
Adopt a sedentary routine to conserve energy

rationale: Sodium reduction, exercise, alcohol limitation, and weight management lower blood pressure; processed foods and inactivity worsen it.

subject: Pediatrics
stem: A nurse reviews an immunization schedule for a child. Which situations warrant delaying or withholding a scheduled vaccine? Select all that apply.

options.text: A severe anaphylactic reaction to a previous dose of the same vaccine
Current moderate to severe acute illness with fever
Known immunocompromise before a live vaccine
A mild upper respiratory infection without fever
Mild soreness at a prior injection site
Current breastfeeding by the mother

rationale: Anaphylaxis to a prior dose, moderate-severe febrile illness, and immunocompromise for live vaccines are true precautions; minor illness and local soreness are not.

subject: Community Health
stem: A nurse conducts a community screening for type 2 diabetes risk. Which client factors increase risk and support screening? Select all that apply.

options.text: Body mass index in the obese range
A first-degree relative with type 2 diabetes
History of gestational diabetes
Physically active with normal weight and no family history
Age under 20 with no other risk factors

rationale: Obesity, family history, and prior gestational diabetes raise type 2 diabetes risk; an active, normal-weight young adult without risk factors is lower risk.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: A nurse assesses factors that may act as barriers to a client's learning during discharge teaching. Which findings represent barriers to learning? Select all that apply.

options.text: Client speaks a language different from the nurse and no interpreter is present
Client reports significant anxiety about going home
Client has uncorrected hearing impairment
Client has a low literacy level with written materials only
Client asks clarifying questions and takes notes
Client has a supportive family member present

rationale: Language mismatch, high anxiety, sensory impairment, and literacy limits impede learning; engagement and support facilitate it.

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Which 3 findings are expected developmental milestones for a healthy 4-year-old child?

options.text: Hops on one foot
Draws a person with several body parts
Uses sentences of four or more words
Ties shoelaces independently
Speaks only single words
Walks unsteadily with a wide-based gait

rationale: Hopping, drawing a multi-part person, and multi-word sentences are typical at 4 years; shoe-tying is later and single words or unsteady gait are earlier or abnormal.

subject: Community Health
stem: Routine cervical cancer screening with a Papanicolaou (Pap) test is generally recommended to begin at age 21 for individuals with a cervix, regardless of sexual history.
rationale: Cervical cancer screening is recommended to start at age 21 irrespective of sexual activity onset.

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Placing a healthy infant to sleep in the prone (on the stomach) position is the recommended way to reduce the risk of sudden infant death syndrome.
rationale: Infants should be placed supine (on the back) to sleep; the prone position increases SIDS risk.

subject: Community Health
stem: For each preventive screening, click to indicate whether it is typically recommended for a healthy adult woman or a healthy older adult of either sex.

rows.text: One-time abdominal aortic aneurysm screening (in men who smoked)

rationale: Mammography and Pap screening target adult women, while DEXA and AAA screening are aimed at older adults.

subject: Community Health
stem: For each life stage, select all anticipatory-guidance topics that a nurse should prioritize (more than one may apply).
rationale: Toddlers need car-seat and fall guidance, adolescents need substance-use screening, and older adults need fall prevention.

subject: Maternity
stem: At a routine visit, the nurse measures the fundal height. By approximately {1} weeks gestation, the fundus is normally expected to reach the level of the {2}.
rationale: The fundus reaches the umbilicus around 20 weeks gestation, a useful marker of expected growth.

subject: Community Health
stem: A home-health nurse visits an older adult. Highlight the findings that indicate a need for further intervention. The client [[walks with a steady gait using a cane]]. There are [[loose electrical cords across the hallway]]. The [[bathroom has grab bars installed]]. Medications are [[stored in unlabeled containers]]. The stairwell is [[poorly lit with no handrail]].

chunks.text: walks with a steady gait using a cane
chunks.feedback: A steady assisted gait is reassuring.

chunks.text: loose electrical cords across the hallway

chunks.feedback: Grab bars are a positive safety feature.
Unlabeled medications risk errors and need intervention.
A poorly lit railless stairwell is a major fall hazard.

rationale: Loose cords, unlabeled medications, and an unsafe stairwell require intervention; assisted steady gait and grab bars are protective.

subject: Maternity
stem: A nurse prepares discharge teaching for a first-time mother and her healthy newborn. Complete the diagram by selecting the teaching priority, actions to teach, and outcomes to monitor.

tokens.text: Place the newborn supine for every sleep
Support the newborn's head when holding
Add rice cereal to bottles at night
Position the newborn prone to prevent choking
Adequate number of wet diapers per day
Steady weight gain after initial loss

rationale: Safe newborn care centers on supine sleep and head support, with hydration and weight gain as key monitored outcomes.

subject: Pediatrics
stem: The nurse reviews milestones with parents. A healthy infant typically sits without support at about [1] and begins to walk independently at about [2].
rationale: Independent sitting emerges around 6 months and independent walking around 12 months.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: A nurse plans structured health-promotion teaching for a client. Place the steps of the teaching process in the correct order.
tokens: Assess the client's learning needs and readiness
Set mutual learning goals with the client
Select and deliver appropriate teaching methods
Evaluate the client's understanding with teach-back
Document the teaching and the client's response
